name: llhttp HTTP message parsing (llhttp_execute state machine)
description:
HARNESS RULES FOR THIS GROUP: (a) the MAIN PATH below runs on every input with the full input, exactly as listed; it is the baseline, the rest of this Logic Group only adds to it. (b) Entries marked 'same core / alternative' reach the same internal code as the main call: never replace the main call with them and never run all of them on every input (fan-out kills exec/s); if used, run at most one of them as an extra step chosen by spare input bits. (c) A configuration switch must never take inputs away from the main path; options that only add code (e.g. detail/verbose output) stay ON. (d) This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers, tests and examples do with the target stays in scope. (e) Nothing the fuzz input can make slow or hang may run on every input: no allocation sized from an untrusted header field, no call with a known library hang (listed below), no callback/selector that aborts the main call for a large share of inputs; the bytes handed to the parser start at a fixed offset (offset 0 when the format has a magic number), so the fuzzer can find magic numbers and header fields.
MAIN PATH (keep on every input; verified in llhttp 9.4.3 (qf-work/src/llhttp-c1) source):
1. Three control bytes at the front: ctrl (parser type + lenient bits), chunk_ctrl (chunk count + finish bit), mode (callback return behaviour); the rest is the HTTP stream.
2. llhttp_settings_init(&settings) and set EVERY callback (src/native/api.h:30-50, llhttp.h settings): span callbacks on_url/on_status/on_method/on_version/on_header_field/on_header_value/on_body/on_protocol/on_chunk_extension_name/on_chunk_extension_value hash their bytes and return -1 (HPE_USER) only on a mode bit plus a content condition; notify callbacks on_message_begin/on_message_complete/on_*_complete/on_chunk_header/on_chunk_complete/on_reset return HPE_PAUSED on one mode bit; on_headers_complete returns 0/1/2/-1 picked by 2 mode bits (api.h:39-47 contract) and reads the getters (llhttp_get_type/http_major/http_minor/method/status_code/upgrade, llhttp_message_needs_eof, llhttp_should_keep_alive). One mode bit may leave the optional on_protocol / on_chunk_extension_* callbacks NULL (CALLBACK_MAYBE skip path).
3. llhttp_init(&parser, type, &settings) with type HTTP_BOTH / HTTP_REQUEST / HTTP_RESPONSE from ctrl.
4. Lenient flags from ctrl bits: llhttp_set_lenient_headers, _chunked_length, _keep_alive, _transfer_encoding, _version, _data_after_close (api.h:234-305).
5. Feed the stream to llhttp_execute in 1..4 chunks (chunk_ctrl); after HPE_PAUSED call llhttp_resume, after HPE_PAUSED_UPGRADE call llhttp_resume_after_upgrade, on any other error read llhttp_get_error_reason / llhttp_get_error_pos / llhttp_errno_name and stop (README.md:186-197).
6. llhttp_finish on a chunk_ctrl bit (README.md:204, api.h:144), then read llhttp_get_errno / get_type / should_keep_alive / get_error_reason.
NEVER call llhttp_set_lenient_header_value_relaxed (api.h:371): in this version it is a library infinite loop. With LENIENT_HEADER_VALUE_RELAXED set and LENIENT_HEADERS clear, any header-value byte that is neither CR/LF nor in RELAXED_HEADER_CHARS bounces between the states header_value_otherwise and header_value_relaxed without consuming input (src/llhttp/http.ts:841-868), so llhttp_execute never returns. The previous LG harness enabled it from one input bit: 65 x 25 s timeouts (all 66 timeout inputs had the bit set), about 27 of the 30 minutes lost.
ADDITIONS on top (spare input bits only): the newer lenient setters llhttp_set_lenient_optional_lf_after_cr, _optional_cr_before_lf, _optional_crlf_after_chunk, _spaces_after_chunk_size (api.h:317-354) from spare bits (they gave the previous LG harness ~140 extra llhttp.c lines); llhttp_reset + a second pass over the same bytes on a spare bit (pipelined messages, api.h:110); llhttp_method_name / llhttp_status_name on the parsed values; parser->data pointing at a per-input context. No artificial payload cap below the libFuzzer max_len.

FEATURE DESCRIPTION (from the Logic Group stage):
llhttp_execute() feeds raw, untrusted network bytes into the generated llhttp state machine (llhttp__internal_execute -> llhttp__internal__run), which parses an HTTP/1.x request or response byte-by-byte (method, URL, version, headers, chunked/content-length bodies, upgrade handling) and invokes user callbacks with pointers/spans into the caller-owned input buffer. Because it directly drives a hand-rolled C state machine over attacker-controlled bytes (header folding, chunked transfer-encoding, content-length vs transfer-encoding conflicts, CR/LF leniency, upgrade/CONNECT handling), it is a classic target for request-smuggling and memory-safety bugs, so exercising it with varied parser types, lenient flags, and chunked/pipelined inputs is security relevant.
- llhttp_execute: target; repeatedly called with attacker-controlled byte chunks to drive llhttp__internal__run through the generated state machine (C).
- llhttp_init: source/lifecycle-setup; selects llhttp_type_t (HTTP_REQUEST / HTTP_RESPONSE / HTTP_BOTH) and installs the llhttp_settings_t callback table that the core calls back into (CALLBACK_MAYBE/SPAN_CALLBACK_MAYBE in api.c) — the type selects different paths through the generated grammar (request-line vs status-line parsing).
- llhttp_settings_init: config; zero-initializes the settings struct so the harness can register only the on_* callbacks needed (on_url, on_header_field/value, on_body, on_headers_complete, on_message_complete, on_chunk_header, etc.), each of which is invoked from inside the core state machine via CALLBACK_MAYBE/SPAN_CALLBACK_MAYBE and can itself return HPE_PAUSED/-1 to redirect control flow.
- llhttp_finish: variant/consumer; called after feeding all bytes to signal EOF, exercising llhttp__after_message_complete / llhttp_message_needs_eof paths for bodies that terminate on connection close (no Content-Length, HTTP/1.0 keep-alive rules).
- llhttp_resume / llhttp_resume_after_upgrade: variants; needed to continue llhttp_execute after a callback returns HPE_PAUSED or after an upgrade/CONNECT message returns HPE_PAUSED_UPGRADE, letting the harness drive multi-call sequences and pipelined requests through the same parser state.
- llhttp_set_lenient_headers / llhttp_set_lenient_chunked_length / llhttp_set_lenient_keep_alive / llhttp_set_lenient_transfer_encoding / llhttp_set_lenient_optional_lf_after_cr / llhttp_set_lenient_optional_cr_before_lf / llhttp_set_lenient_optional_crlf_after_chunk / llhttp_set_lenient_spaces_after_chunk_size: config; each flips a lenient_flags bit checked throughout the generated grammar (c_test_lenient_flags_* callees) and in llhttp__after_headers_complete, selecting stricter vs. relaxed parsing branches (request-smuggling-relevant divergent paths) for the same input bytes.
- llhttp_reset: config/lifecycle; resets parser state while preserving type/settings/lenient flags, enabling the harness to parse multiple independent messages with the same configuration in one fuzz run (pipelining).
The input space the harness should vary: (1) the raw HTTP bytes passed to llhttp_execute, ideally split into multiple chunks/calls to exercise partial-parse/resume paths; (2) llhttp_type_t passed to llhttp_init (HTTP_REQUEST, HTTP_RESPONSE, HTTP_BOTH) which chooses request-line vs status-line grammar; (3) which lenient_* flags are enabled before executing, each toggling a distinct branch in the core (header token validation, chunked-length vs content-length conflict handling, optional CR/LF, spaces after chunk size, data after Connection:close); (4) callback return values from the registered llhttp_settings_t callbacks (0, 1, 2, -1, HPE_PAUSED) which alter control flow inside llhttp__after_headers_complete/llhttp__after_message_complete and can trigger llhttp_pause/resume paths; (5) presence/absence of chunked Transfer-Encoding vs Content-Length headers and upgrade/CONNECT requests, which select between body_identity, body_identity_eof, chunk_size_start and the HPE_PAUSED_UPGRADE early-exit paths in llhttp__after_headers_complete.
